rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 6:"This module holds that reflex off." — harm the rule prevents: the training narrating its own pedagogical mechanism instead of the student's repo/agent/task/artifact/decision, reading as author-interesting orientation the reader didn't come for. Present here: grammatical subject is literally "This module", the section (## Diagnose first, fix later) is not one of the exempt signposting names, and the deletion test shows the surrounding sentences do NOT join cleanly without it (it supplies the reason the next sentence's "earn the validation" makes sense) — so a subject swap, not a cut, is the fix. A close neighbour, "The arc is test → learn → encode" one bullet down, was checked against the same test and held: its subject is also training-shaped, but it names the operative M4/M5/M6 framework the student uses in the next two minutes rather than describing the curriculum's own sequencing, which is the harm this rule targets — kept as PASS, flagged here for the maintainer as the closer of the two calls.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast off "this module" onto the student or the artifact: "You hold that reflex off" or "That reflex stays off here" preserves the connective logic (why the next sentence's failures get to "earn the validation") without the training narrating its own design.
